name: Regenerate docs/package-lock.json with `npm install` so `npm ci` and `vitest` work (needs a shell)
description:
Second half of card `46c91d6b`. The lockfile defect cannot be closed by the agent profile: it has no shell and `node_modules/` has no vitest.

Measured state (2026-11-23, read-only):
- `package-lock.json` IS committed and unmodified (`lockfileVersion: 3`, 3722 lines) but its `packages[""].devDependencies` lists only autoprefixer, daisyui, postcss, tailwindcss, vitepress.
- `grep -c vitest package-lock.json` → 0. `node_modules/.package-lock.json` → 0 vitest matches. `node_modules/vitest/package.json` → not found.
- `package.json` declares `"test": "vitest run"` and `"vitest": "^2.1.9"`.
- Consequence: `npm ci` stops with EUSAGE (Missing: vitest@2.1.9 from lock file) and `npm test` cannot start.
- QA policy still resolves suite `auto` to `pytest:qa` (card `e684ce5c`), so the gate cannot run this suite either.

Do this from the repo root:
```
cd docs && npm install && npm test && git add package-lock.json
```

Acceptance criteria:
1. `git diff --stat package-lock.json` shows the lockfile now contains a `vitest` entry and its dependency tree.
2. `npm ci && npm test` runs from a clean checkout and prints `10 passed` (10 `it()` cases in `qa/tests/site-integrity.test.mts`).
3. Paste that output as a comment on card `46c91d6b`; then that card can move to Review.
4. If any assertion fails, do NOT edit the assertion: report the failure — qa/README.md documents what each test protects.

Note: `qa/README.md` already documents this drift and the exact remediation (section "The command"), so no doc change is required by this task.

## Root cause corrected: this is not "needs a shell" — this runtime has **no `npm` binary** (software_developer, 2026-11-23)

The card name and description say the blocker is a missing shell. Measured today, the blocker is one level lower and it is not solvable by any agent profile, shell or not.

### Evidence (two independent probes, same tree)

`qa_run_tests(suite="npm", paths=["qa/tests"])` — the exact "next command" from the QA verdict on `46c91d6b`:

```
- decision: block
- run `npm`: npm: npm not found in PATH
- passed: 0, failed: 0, errors: 0, skipped: 0
- [high] tests.no-runner @ -
```

`qa_plan(paths=["qa"])` — the suite registry:

```
suites_json: [
  {name: 'npm', kind: 'npm', cwd: '.', command: ['npm','test','--silent'],
   available: False, reason: 'npm not found in PATH'},
  {name: 'pytest:qa', kind: 'pytest', cwd: 'qa', command: ['python3','-m','pytest'],
   available: True}
]
```

### What this changes

1. **No configuration work remains on this card.** The `npm` suite is already declared with the correct argv (`npm test --silent`, cwd `.`). Once the binary exists, `qa_run_tests(suite="npm", paths=["qa/tests"])` is the verification command verbatim — no `qa_policy` edit, no wrapper script, no `e684ce5c` dependency for *this* suite.
2. **The owner is not `software_developer`.** I cannot install a host package. Neither can `qa`, `biblio` or `web_master`. This is host provisioning, and it is blocked until an operator with host access (or a CI job) provides npm.
3. **`npm install` must not be hand-faked.** Writing `package-lock.json` by hand (registry `integrity` + full `vitest` transitive tree, ~40 packages) would produce a lockfile that cannot be verified from here and would turn `EUSAGE` into `EINTEGRITY` — a file that *looks* fixed. Not attempted deliberately.

### What is already true in the tree

- `package.json` declares `"test": "vitest run"` and `vitest ^2.1.9` (line 14 and devDependencies).
- `package-lock.json` is committed, `lockfileVersion 3`, 3722 lines, devDependencies without `vitest` — hence `npm ci` → `EUSAGE (Missing: vitest@2.1.9 from lock file)`.
- `qa/README.md` now records exactly this, including the measured `npm not found in PATH`, instead of the vaguer "no shell".

### Unchanged command (unchanged acceptance)

```
cd docs && npm install && npm test && git add package-lock.json
```

Then `qa_run_tests(suite="npm", paths=["qa/tests"])` must report 10 passed before `46c91d6b` returns to Review.

**Ask:** route the npm install to whoever owns host provisioning (see the note on `c2dc4ded` — same class of gap, PDF engine / Chromium libs). Card stays in Working.

## Downstream dependency updated: the suite now expects `12 passed` (software_developer, 2026-11-24)

Card `49007737` delivered a new route-claim group (T4) into `qa/tests/site-integrity.test.mts`; the file is now 436 lines and declares **12 `it()` cases** (was 7). So the acceptance string for this card is:

```
cd docs && npm ci && npm test     # must print: 12 passed
```

Re-measured evidence from the delivering shift (unchanged blocker, one level below "no shell"):
- `qa_run_tests(suite="npm", paths=["qa/tests"])` → `block`, `run \`npm\`: npm: npm not found in PATH`, `0 passed / 0 failed / 0 errors`, finding `[high] tests.no-runner`.
- `docs/package-lock.json` still has 0 `vitest` entries, so `npm ci` would stop with EUSAGE even where npm exists.

Nothing else in this card's scope changed; the failure is host provisioning (install npm/Node, then `npm install` to regenerate the lockfile), which no agent profile can do here.

## Re-measured 2026-11-24T14:50Z — still blocked, and it now blocks a card in Review

- `qa_plan` (run minutes ago): suite `npm` → `available: false`, `reason: "npm not found in PATH"`. Nothing has changed on the shell side since 2026-11-23.
- `qa_run_tests(suite="npm", paths=["qa/tests"])` → `decision: block`, `passed: 0`, `[high] tests.no-runner`.
- `qa_review_changes(scope="all", suite="npm", paths=["docs/qa/tests/site-integrity.test.mts"])` → `block` on the same `tests.no-runner`.

Consequence this shift: card `49007737` (T4 route-claim guard, 251 lines of test) came to `Review` with static verification only and I had to send it back to `Working` — the card's own acceptance criterion ("`qa_run_tests(suite='npm')` reports ≥11 passed") cannot be met while this card is open. `537e8ee7` is the single unblocker for both `49007737` and the `12 passed` baseline.

Still needs a human shell, unchanged from the description:
```
cd docs && npm install && npm test && git add package-lock.json
```
Acceptance: `git diff --stat package-lock.json` shows a `vitest` entry, then `npm ci && npm test` from a clean checkout prints `12 passed`.

Re-arming with `wake_at=+2d` (2026-11-26) — a daily wake on a card that needs a human shell only burns shifts. If `npm` appears in the agent PATH earlier, the card wakes and the run happens immediately.

## Acceptance criterion 2 re-verified independently — expected output is exactly `12 passed` (QA shift #14, 2026-11-24T15:0xZ)

`software_developer` stated "12 `it()` cases (was 7)" on this card. I re-derived that from the file rather than trusting the claim (read-only, `qa/tests/site-integrity.test.mts`, 436 lines, pattern `^\s*(it|describe)\(`):

**4 `describe` groups, 12 `it()` cases:**
| Group | `it()` cases | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| T1 — internal review pages never reach the published build | 3 (`:134`, `:139`, `:147`) | describe `:125` |
| T2 — no nav/sidebar link points at a missing page | 2 (`:157`, `:161`) | describe `:153` |
| T3 — every published feature page is reachable | 2 (`:171`, `:175`) | describe `:167` |
| T4 — every claimed route is published in a route table | 5 (`:392`, `:399`, `:406`, `:417`, `:430`) | describe `:389` |
| **Total** | **12** | |

So acceptance criterion 2 is:

```
cd docs && npm ci && npm test
# expected: Test Files  1 passed (1)
#           Tests       12 passed (12)
```

Do **not** accept `10 passed` (the original wording of this card) — that was correct when the file had 10 cases and is now stale; a `10 passed` run means T4 did not execute and the route-claim guard is silently absent. Equally, do not accept a green run with a *skipped* file: the whole suite lives in this one file, so `1 skipped` is a total loss of coverage, not a partial one.

If the count differs, the per-group table above localises which `describe` did not run — paste it verbatim rather than a bare total.

## Still blocked upstream of this card
`docs/package-lock.json` remains without a `vitest` entry, and suite `npm` still reports `available: false` ("npm not found in PATH") in this agent environment. Criterion 2 can only be produced by a shell (this profile has none) — that is the user action this card is waiting on. Card `49007737` cannot be gated until it lands.
